 ATP Finals Best Bets for Sunday, November 15 + WTA Finals Prediction: Svitolina vs. Andreeva
 Why there's no bet on Andreeva-Svitolina, and where the value is in Sunday's ATP Finals.
 By Zachary Cohen - November 14, 2026 5586 
 X Facebook Email 
 The ATP Finals and WTA Finals both wrap up their seasons this month, and Sunday gives bettors a lot to work with. Below are my best bets for the ATP Finals matchups on November 15. I also dive into the WTA Finals championship match between Elina Svitolina and Mirra Andreeva. 
 MORE: Check out Gill Alexander’s best bets on our Pro Picks page! 
 ATP Finals Best Bets for Sunday, November 15 
 PARLAY: Alexander Zverev ML vs. Rafael Jodar & Ben Shelton ML vs. Arthur Fils (+117)
 There isn’t much for me on the Sunday card at the ATP Finals, and I may focus far more on Challengers than on the year-end event. The field in Turin is insanely weak, and there’s almost more intrigue at the lower levels of tennis this week. Still, when I can, I’ll do my best to get you plays. We’ll start by parlaying the favorites on Sunday.
 Zverev might be struggling heading into the tournament, but it’s hard to pinpoint Jodar’s advantages in this matchup. Zverev is the better server and returner, which gives him an edge in the most important areas of the sport. The German’s backhand will be the biggest weapon on the court, and the forehand is no longer a weakness. He has been hitting with far more conviction from that wing, which helped him win two majors in 2026. Add his massive edge in experience, and this is a match he should win.
 Shelton probably faces more of a challenge. At times, Fils has looked like a top-five player this season, but the Frenchman isn’t as consistent as he needs to be. Shelton comes in with much better form, having reached the final of last week’s Rolex Paris Masters and put up a good fight against Carlos Alcaraz. He’s also 2-0 against Fils on indoor hard courts, and it’s easy to see why. He’s simply a much better server, and that should ultimately be the difference on Sunday. It won’t hurt to have a little extra motivation, either, with Juan Carlos Ferrero in Turin to work with him for the first time.
 WTA Finals Championship Match: Elina Svitolina vs. Mirra Andreeva
 As lame as it is, I don’t have a play for the last match of the WTA Finals. We’re riding a pre-tournament future on Andreeva, so we’re simply hoping that cashes. I won’t be hedging, since the last couple of weeks have been strong. Still, with +235 available on the Ukrainian, I wouldn’t blame anyone for shedding some risk.
 I do expect Andreeva to win. The 19-year-old is scorching hot, hasn’t dropped a set in this event, and has every part of her game working. My issue is the price. Andreeva beat Svitolina easily in group play, yet she was only -189 to win that match at DraftKings. She’s -267 now. That’s a big move based on one result, especially since the first set of that meeting could have gone either way.
 Still, Andreeva is the better returner, and her baseline game is levels above. She’s also a rapidly improving server, so I’m not sure Svitolina has the edge there, either. It would realistically take an Andreeva meltdown for her to lose, but it can’t be ruled out. Jessica Pegula said what she said for a reason!
 Added Plays
 I usually have A LOT MORE on the Pro Picks page . These plays count towards my record and have been a big part of my success this season. Make sure you check them out. I’ll probably add a few more over there, so refresh that page throughout the day if you’re looking for action. That’s also where I put my Challenger-level plays, as well as picks for lower level ATP and WTA events.
